newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

SIERRA LEONE, Sept 23 - Freetown - no labour problems. Two vessels discharging at berth of which 1 rice, 1 clinker. 1 Vessel anchored under arrest. 5 vessels due of which 4 dischargers (2 containers, 1 rice, 1 containers/vehicles), 1 mill feed loader. For the sake of security, vessels must endeavour to be in/out of port before 1900 hrs.

SOUTH AFRICA, Sept 23 - Richards Bay - general cargo berths working normally. Bulk import berths sulphur/coking coal berths extremely congested with delays of 20-30 days. Bulk export berths working normally. Bulk coal berths - congestion expected this week. 10 vessels due 26-27/9 and depending on loading performance at coal terminal, berthing delays of 36-48 hours expected. Further 6 vessels due 29/9, berthing delays expected to continue until beginning of October. Durban - container terminal delays of up to 36 hours. Point, New Pier/Maydon Wharf berths working normally. Maize terminal (Maydon Wharf 8) 3 maize loaders for Sept, 5 for October. Citrus terminal tapering off as season closing. Bunker supplies tight - delays in supplying bunkers expected due to bunching of vessels. Dry/floating dock fully booked for Sept and 60% booked for october. East London - general cargo/combi terminal berths extremely busy but no delays. Dry-dock fully booked for Sept and first two weeks of october, thereafter open for bookings. Copper moving in small parcels of 2,500 tonnes per month to far east. Elevator busy but no delays. Gas oil pipeline under utilised. Log loaders 15,000 cubic metres on hand awaiting shipment. Scrap steel 5,500 tonnes on hand awaiting shipment. Wheat 1 vessel due mid-October. Port Elizabeth - working normally with 7 vessels in port. No delays on general, ore, tanker, or container berths. One citrus vessel in port, two more expected then season over. Cape Town - breakbulk berths no delays, vessels working on arrival. Container terminal no delays expected for coming week. Two new gantry cranes fully operational. Bunker berths no delays foreseen for coming week. Dry-dock and repair quay fully occupied, booking essential. Saldanha Bay working normally.

YEMEN, Sept 23 - Hodeidah - all berths occupied except nos. 1, 4 and 8. 5 vessels berthed of which 1 timber, 1 steel, 2 containers, 1 passenger. 4 vessels anchored of which 1 bulk wheat, 1 wheat flour, 1 general cargo, 1 general cargo/containers. Berthing delays general cargo up to 2 days. Bagged cargoes up to 4 days. Bulk cargo up to 6 days. Containers up to 1 day. Mokha - one vessel berthed discharging wheat flour, No vessels anchored, no berthing delays.
